description: Official dashboard for the Centrifugo real-time messaging server (https://centrifugal.dev). Covers connections, client commands, delivery, recovery, server API, proxies, consumers, brokers and Go runtime, plus collapsed rows for Centrifugo PRO metrics. Uses histogram metrics only — Prometheus Summaries are deprecated in Centrifugo v6.8.1 and removed in v7.

panels.description: Client connections across all selected nodes.
panels.title: Connections

panels.description: Unique users. Uniqueness is per node, so a user whose connections land on several nodes is counted once per node. With one connection per user the sum is exact. See 'Users per node' in the Connections row for exact per-node values.
panels.title: Users

panels.description: Active channel subscriptions across selected nodes.
panels.title: Subscriptions

panels.description: Channels with at least one subscriber. Counted per node, so a channel with subscribers on several nodes is counted once per node — in a cluster this is an upper bound, not a distinct count, and a broadcast channel contributes once per node. See 'Channels per node' in the Connections row for exact per-node values.
panels.title: Channels

panels.description: Cluster size as seen by nodes. A value that flaps means nodes are not seeing each other reliably over the broker.
panels.title: Nodes in cluster

panels.description: Uptime of the most recently started node — drops to zero on restarts, crashes and rolling deploys.
panels.title: Min uptime

panels.description: Accepted client connections per second. A sustained high value with flat 'Connections' means clients are reconnecting in a loop.
panels.title: Connect rate

panels.description: Errors returned to clients per second, all methods and codes.
panels.title: Client error rate

panels.description: Golden signal — throughput. Client commands, real-time transport frames and node↔broker messages on one scale.
panels.title: Traffic

panels.description: Golden signal — errors. Note client reply errors include expected application-level errors; look at the per-code breakdown before alerting on this.
panels.title: Errors

panels.description: Golden signal — latency. Quantile selectable with the Quantile variable. Percentiles are computed from histogram buckets, so they aggregate correctly across nodes.
panels.title: Latency (q=$quantile)

panels.description: Currently open client connections per transport.
panels.title: Connections inflight by transport

panels.description: New connections per second. Compare with the inflight panel: high accept rate + flat inflight = reconnect storm.
panels.title: Connections accepted rate by transport

panels.description: Requests refused because the node reached `client.connection_limit`. Anything above zero means clients are being turned away — scale out or raise the limit.
panels.title: Connections refused by node limit

panels.description: Per-node connection count — the panel to check for unbalanced load across the cluster. The Overview 'Connections' tile carries the fleet total and its trend.
panels.title: Connections per node

panels.description: Unique users connected to each node. Exact per node — unlike the summed Overview tile, which counts a user once per node they are connected to.
panels.title: Users per node

panels.description: Active subscriptions on each node. Subscriptions are per connection, so the Overview tile's fleet sum is exact.
panels.title: Subscriptions per node

panels.description: Channels with at least one subscriber on each node. Exact per node — unlike the summed Overview tile, which counts a channel once per node holding subscribers for it.
panels.title: Channels per node

panels.description: Active subscriptions across the selected nodes. Compare with 'Connections inflight' to see how many channels an average client holds.
panels.title: Subscriptions inflight

panels.description: Unsubscribes initiated by the server. See the [unsubscribe codes](https://centrifugal.dev/docs/server/codes#client-unsubscribe-codes) reference.
panels.title: Server-side unsubscribes by code

panels.description: Disconnects initiated by the server. See the [disconnect codes](https://centrifugal.dev/docs/server/codes#client-disconnect-codes) reference.
panels.title: Server-side disconnects by code

panels.description: Close frames sent by the server, by transport and close code (Centrifugo v6.8.4+). Only server-sent codes are counted — client-supplied codes are ignored to bound cardinality.
panels.title: Outgoing close frames by code

panels.description: Client protocol commands per second. Derived from the histogram companion metric — the deprecated Summary is not used.
panels.title: Command rate by method

panels.description: Errors returned in replies. Codes 100–113 are Centrifugo's built-in client errors ([reference](https://centrifugal.dev/docs/server/codes#client-error-codes)); other values are custom codes returned by your proxy handlers.
panels.title: Reply error rate by method and code

panels.description: Time to process a client command, including any proxy call it triggers. Spikes on `subscribe`/`connect` usually point at proxy latency — check the Proxy row.

targets.expr:
histogram_quantile($quantile, sum by (le, method) (rate(centrifugo_client_command_duration_seconds_histogram_bucket{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance"}[$__rate_interval])))
or
histogram_quantile($quantile, sum by (method)(rate(centrifugo_client_command_duration_seconds_histogram{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance"}[$__rate_interval])))

panels.title: Command duration (q=$quantile) by method

panels.description: Percentile spread across all methods. A p99 far above p50 means a small share of commands is much slower — usually proxy calls or history lookups on a hot channel.
panels.title: Command duration percentiles (all methods)

panels.description: Share of commands that returned an error, per method.

targets.expr:
100 * (
sum by (method)(rate(centrifugo_client_num_reply_errors{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance"}[$__rate_interval]))
/
sum by (method)(rate(centrifugo_client_command_duration_seconds_histogram_count{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance"}[$__rate_interval]))
)
or
100 * (
sum by (method)(rate(centrifugo_client_num_reply_errors{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance"}[$__rate_interval]))
/
sum by (method)(histogram_count(rate(centrifugo_client_command_duration_seconds_histogram{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance"}[$__rate_interval])))
)

panels.title: Command error ratio by method

panels.description: Round-trip time between a server ping and the client pong — an end-to-end health signal for the client's network and its ability to process frames in time.

targets.expr:
histogram_quantile(0.5, sum by (le, transport) (rate(centrifugo_client_ping_pong_duration_seconds_bucket{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance"}[$__rate_interval])))
or
histogram_quantile(0.5, sum by (transport)(rate(centrifugo_client_ping_pong_duration_seconds{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance"}[$__rate_interval])))

histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le, transport) (rate(centrifugo_client_ping_pong_duration_seconds_bucket{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance"}[$__rate_interval])))
or
histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (transport)(rate(centrifugo_client_ping_pong_duration_seconds{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance"}[$__rate_interval])))

histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (le, transport) (rate(centrifugo_client_ping_pong_duration_seconds_bucket{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance"}[$__rate_interval])))
or
histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (transport)(rate(centrifugo_client_ping_pong_duration_seconds{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance"}[$__rate_interval])))

panels.title: Client ping/pong latency by transport

panels.description: Protocol frames pushed to clients, by frame type — `push_publication`, `push_join`, `push_leave`, `push_disconnect`, `server_ping` and the reply frames named after the command they answer.
panels.title: Frames sent by frame type

panels.description: Protocol frames received from clients, by frame type — `connect`, `subscribe`, `publish`, `history`, `presence`, `rpc`, `client_pong` and so on.
panels.title: Frames received by frame type

panels.description: Uncompressed payload bytes written to client connections. Framing overhead is not counted and neither is transport compression, so this is a lower bound on real egress rather than bytes on the wire.
panels.title: Bandwidth out by transport

panels.description: Uncompressed payload bytes read from client connections, excluding framing overhead.
panels.title: Bandwidth in by transport

panels.description: Size of whole protocol frames read from client connections. A frame may batch several commands — a client's reconnect frame typically carries connect plus every subscribe — so this is not derivable from bandwidth-in or the per-command counters. `websocket.message_size_limit` bounds the whole frame, so size it from this panel's tail rather than an average.

targets.expr:
histogram_quantile($quantile, sum by (le, transport) (rate(centrifugo_transport_frame_size_bucket{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance"}[$__rate_interval])))
or
histogram_quantile($quantile, sum by (transport)(rate(centrifugo_transport_frame_size{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance"}[$__rate_interval])))

panels.title: Frame size (q=$quantile) by transport

panels.description: Messages published by this node into the broker (publication, join, leave, control).
panels.title: Node → broker messages by type

panels.description: Messages consumed by this node from the broker. A publication is delivered to every node that currently holds subscribers for the channel, so cluster-wide totals grow with fan-out across nodes; control messages go to all nodes.

panels.description: Time from publish to the message being picked up from the broker. In a distributed setup this depends on clock sync between nodes (run NTP) — even then, the trend is meaningful.

panels.description: Time to deliver a message to all subscribers on the node. Growing together with message rate is the classic signal to scale out.
